name: French Republic

areaKm2.note: Metropolitan France: World Bank land area 538,950 km2 (low); total area incl. inland water ~551,500 km2 (mid); world_1960 France polygon computes to ~550,900 km2. Overseas departments and territories excluded.

population.note: OWID population 1989 = 56,685,081 (metropolitan, mid); COW NMC v7 tpop 1989 = 56,423k (low); World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 1989 = 57,943,062 incl. overseas departments (high).

urbanization.note: OWID/HYDE urban share France 1989 = 74.1%; World Bank SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS 1989 = 73.9%.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), France entry, as transcribed at the cited page: ACTIVE some 466,300 (13,300 women, 240,100 conscripts) incl 3,600 Central Staff, 8,700 Service de sante, 2,000 Service des essences; Army 292,500, Navy 65,500, Air Force 94,100. Gendarmerie 87,200 excluded (COW milper 558k and World Bank 554k include it).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), France entry, as transcribed at the cited page: reserves earmarked for mobilisation 353,000 (Army 267,000, Navy 28,000, Air 58,000). High adds the 130,000 Gendarmerie reserve. Potential reserve 1,190,500 (Army 915,000) is the wider pool, see mobilizable.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the infantry P roles: Navy, Air Force, strategic forces (18,700) and Army armour, artillery, ALAT, engineers, signals, logistics, schools and staffs = 466,300 minus ~60,000 infantry (reconstruction from the MB order of battle).

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogue: france-1939 snapshot (5.0M mobilised of ~41M in 1939-40 = 0.12; WWI 0.21 ceiling), scaled down for 1989: the MB potential reserve of 1,190,500 plus active 466,300 = ~1.66M (0.03 of population) is the organised pool; total-war ratio set at 0.07-0.14 because 12-month conscription kept trained cohorts available.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), France entry, as transcribed at the cited page: 1st Army armoured divisions each with 2 mech and 1 APC infantry regiment (~6 armd div = ~18 regt), 2 inf div with 3 inf regt each, plus the 2 APC inf regt of the light armoured division; ~26 battalion-size regiments at ~900-1,100. Reconstruction from the order of battle; MB gives no personnel by arm.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training). Evidence: 12-month conscripts (240,100 of 466,300); regular cadres

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1989-1990 (data as at 1 June 1989), France entry, as transcribed at the cited page: FAR 11th para div (6 para inf), 9th marine div (2 inf), 27th mountain div (6 mtn inf), Foreign Legion (8,500: 4 inf, 1 para), 12 overseas marine infantry regiments, corps/independent para and inf regiments: ~36 regiments at ~800-1,000. Reconstruction.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: trained staff system and successful African interventions (Kolwezi 1978, Chad 1983-87); 1st Army planned as a national reserve outside NATO integrated command, coordination with NATO only by agreement (Valentin-Ferber 1974)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: national conscript army for the 1st Army; professional FAR, Legion and marine units with strong identity

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: peacetime conscripts; conscripts could not be sent abroad without volunteering; professional units motivated

weapons.note: Anchor: towards 9 (1985). Evidence: Exocet, Milan/HOT, ASMP stand-off missile, AU-F-1; AMX-30 tanks and no MLRS

armor.note: Anchor: between 8 (rolled homogeneous armour) and 9 (composite). Evidence: AMX-30/AMX-30B2 with rolled steel, light protection; Leclerc not yet

ships.note: Anchor: towards 9 (nuclear subs, Aegis). Evidence: 6 SSBN, 4 Rubis SSN, two CATOBAR carriers; no Aegis-class area defence

fortification.note: Anchor: towards 9 (hardened shelters). Evidence: hardened IRBM silos at Albion, hardened command centres (Taverny, Mont Verdun), aircraft shelters

logistics.note: Anchor: towards 9 (containerised, airlift). Evidence: C-160/C-130/DC-8 airlift, KC-135F tankers, prepositioned African bases; limited strategic sealift

communications.note: Anchor: towards 9 (satellite comms, data links). Evidence: Syracuse I military satellite payloads on Telecom 1 (1984-88), RITA automatic integrated trunk network in the Army

isr.note: Anchor: between 8 (radar) and 9 (satellites). Evidence: Atlantic MR, C-160 Gabriel ELINT, Mirage F-1CR; no imaging satellite (Helios 1995) and no AWACS (E-3F 1991)

air.note: Anchor: air 9 = 1985. Evidence: Mirage 2000C/N in service; Mirage III/5 and Crusader legacy

cyber.note: Anchor: cyber 9 = 1990 networks. Evidence: DGSE/GCR SIGINT computer centres, military data networks; no documented offensive network capability in 1989

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS: France 1989 = 2.92%, 1982 = 3.22%. High allows for the NATO definition including the Gendarmerie (~3.7%, not fetched). Peacetime.

industrialShare.note: World Bank industry incl. construction value added: France 1989 = 24.2%, 1982 = 26.2%.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) France 1989 = 5.7%. Share 5.7% (range 4.5-7.0%) -> 0.943 (0.93-0.955).

annualCohort.note: World Bank SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y FRA 1989 = 8.17% of males aged 15-19 (male population 28,165,411); applied to both sexes of the metropolitan population 56.7M (female share assumed equal) / 5 = ~926,000 persons per year (~460,000 males; MB: 240,100 conscripts under arms).

helicopters.note: Educated guess: Aerospatiale Marignane (Gazelle, Puma/Super Puma, Dauphin, Ecureuil), one of the largest helicopter lines outside the US/USSR.

air_defense.note: Educated guess: Roland (Euromissile) and Crotale (Thomson-CSF) fire units, battery equivalents, export lines included.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: French road network ~800,000 km (routes nationales ~28,000 km incl. ~6,500 km autoroutes, departmental ~350,000, communal ~420,000).

railKm.note: World Bank rail lines first value 1995 = 31,997 km (low); SNCF route length in 1989 was ~34,000 km before the 1990s closures. Grade C (series starts after the snapshot).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Marseille-Fos, Le Havre, Dunkirk, Rouen, Nantes-Saint-Nazaire, Bordeaux, Brest, Toulon, Cherbourg, Lorient.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: French-flag merchant fleet ~4-5M grt in 1989 (down from ~11M in 1980), x1.5 to dwt.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: the 1st Army and FAR planned to fight in southern Germany 300-500 km from depots in eastern France; African interventions supplied by air over 3,000-5,000 km.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses in France (~300,000 in 1989, sport and farm), no military transport role.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS (Kristensen and Korda) via OWID: France 1989 = 410 warheads. Delivery (MB 1989-90): 96 SLBM in 6 SSBN (M-4 TN-70/71 MIRV, M-20 TN-60), 18 S-3D, Mirage IVP and 2000N with ASMP, Jaguar/Super Etendard AN-52, 32 Pluton. High = later Norris and Kristensen estimates peaking near 540 in 1991-92.

basesAbroad.name: FFA HQ Baden-Baden, FRG (2nd Corps, 3 armd div)

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified cities, population support and a national conscript army; no harsh-climate depth. Forces in the FRG fight at 1.0.

notes: Snapshot date mid-1989 (IISS Military Balance 1989-1990, data as at 1 June 1989), the last pre-1990 year of the Cold War force. France was a NATO member outside the integrated military command (since 1966); its 1st Army (3 corps) and Rapid Action Force (FAR, 47,000) were national, with agreed contingency plans for engagement alongside CENTAG. Population convention: metropolitan France (OWID 56.7M); overseas departments and territories (DOM-TOM, ~1.3M) excluded and their garrisons listed as basesAbroad. Personnel: active = armed forces 466,300 excl. Gendarmerie 87,200 (paramilitary); earmarked reserves 353,000 = trainedReserves. Infantry P roles are a reconstruction from regiment counts (French regiments are battalion size); everything else supportPersonnel. Abroad (MB 1989-90): FRG 52,700 (3 armd div with 570 MBT), Berlin 2,700, Djibouti 3,650, Antilles-Guyana 8,200, Indian Ocean 3,300, New Caledonia 9,500, Polynesia 5,400, Chad 1,700, Senegal 1,150, CAR 1,200, Cote d'Ivoire 920, Gabon 550, UNIFIL 530. The MB edition was read from a full-text transcription at samlib.ru (cited URL). Weakest values: merchant tonnage, wartime production and the infantry split (reconstructions/educated guesses).
